d.ram: {0} GB in {1} module(s), running at {2} MT/s
f.cpu: Open Task Manager and close the busy process.
f.ram: Close apps or browser tabs, disable startup programs, or add memory.
f.ramsize: 8 GB is the practical minimum for Windows 11.
f.diskspace: Free up space: Settings > System > Storage.
f.diskhealth: Back up your data now: the drive reports problems.
f.uptime: Restart your PC: it clears many slowdowns.
d.reboot: Windows is waiting for a restart
f.startup: Disable some in Task Manager > Startup.
f.devices: Device Manager: update or reinstall the driver.
f.events: Event Viewer > Windows Logs: look for the sources above.
d.crashes: {0} crash(es) or sudden shutdown(s) in 7 days
f.crashes: Check drivers, temperatures and the power supply; run 'sfc /scannow'.
f.diskerrors: Back up your data and run 'chkdsk /f'; consider replacing the drive.
d.noav: Windows Defender is not active (third-party antivirus?)
f.defender: Windows Security > Virus & threat protection: turn real-time protection on.
f.sigs: Run Windows Update or update Windows Security.
f.firewall: Windows Security > Firewall: turn it back on.
f.secureboot: Enable Secure Boot in the BIOS/UEFI (needed for Windows 11 and many anti-cheats).
f.tpm: Enable TPM / fTPM / PTT in the BIOS (needed for Windows 11).
f.activation: Settings > System > Activation. A new PC should come activated.
d.nobloat: No known trial or promotional software found
f.bloat: Uninstall what you don't need: Settings > Apps.
d.single: A single module in a multi-slot machine
f.single: Add a matching second module for about twice the memory bandwidth.
f.xmp: Enable XMP/EXPO in the BIOS to reach full memory speed.
f.batwear: A new laptop should show almost no wear: the battery or the PC may be used or refurbished.
f.hdd: An SSD makes Windows much faster. Consider upgrading.
f.noadapter: Check the cable, turn Wi-Fi on (airplane mode?) or restart the adapter.
f.apipa: Restart your router, then run 'ipconfig /release' and 'ipconfig /renew'.
f.gwdown: Local problem: check the cable or Wi-Fi, or restart the router.
f.gwweak: Unstable link to the router: move closer or use a cable.
f.wifi: Move closer to the router, use 5 GHz or Ethernet.
f.noint: No internet access: restart the box and check with your provider.
f.lossy: Very unstable connection (packet loss): router, cable or provider.
f.dnsslow: Switch to a faster DNS (1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8).
f.captive: Open a browser: a sign-in page may be required.
f.https: A firewall, VPN or proxy blocks HTTPS.
f.proxy: If you don't use one: Settings > Network > Proxy.
f.speed: Try Ethernet, restart the box, check for devices hogging bandwidth.
d.v_local: LOCAL problem: the PC cannot reach its router
d.v_isp: The router answers but the internet does not: box or provider problem
d.v_dns: Internet works but names do not resolve: DNS problem
f.v_local: Check Wi-Fi/cable, restart the router, run 'ipconfig /renew'.
f.v_isp: Restart the box for 30 s; otherwise contact your provider.
ui.tagline: PC & network health check — built for brand-new computers
ui.welcome: Click “Scan my PC”. The scan takes about a minute. Just bought a computer? Look at the “New-PC checks” section: it reveals worn batteries, slow memory, unwanted preinstalled software and activation problems. Then use “Screen test” to look for dead pixels.
ui.screentest_hint: Dead-pixel test. Click or press any key for the next colour. Press Esc to exit.
ui.privacy: 100 % local: nothing is sent anywhere except the network tests (ping, DNS, a small web request).
ui.not_admin: Not running as administrator: a few checks are limited.
ui.allgood: Nothing needs your attention. This PC looks healthy.
